speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education beyond increasing salaries for teachers, what other new measures are being introduced to reduce burnout and improve their work-life balance.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry is considering other measures besides pay increase to enhance the working conditions for teachers including concerns over workload and long hours, such as adding more staff.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) apart from salary increment, whether the Ministry has also looked into ways to ease teachers' workloads and improve their mental well-being in order to attract and retain talents; and (b) whether the Ministry will be working with relevant agencies to ensure that the salary increment and benefits will also apply to MOE-seconded teachers in special education schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE is mindful that the quality of education depends on the strength of our teaching force, and teachers' well-being is critically important to our mission to teach, inspire and nurture future generations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE values our teachers, and pays close attention to their well-being and work-life balance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many of our dedicated teachers go above and beyond the call of duty for our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This allows teachers to focus their time on student-centric work, including CCAs and counselling.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools have also implemented more flexible work arrangements for teachers where feasible, while maintaining the duty of care towards students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This includes holding virtual or hybrid afternoon meetings where meaningful and effective and allowing teachers to leave school when they have no further duties that require them to be in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers who require greater flexibility in work hours can also apply for part-time teaching arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools' Staff Well-Being Committees have also been provided with more resources to enhance staff well-being, such as additional Staff Welfare Funds and in-house curated resources to help them organise meaningful programmes for staff.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers may also take part in well-being workshops, talks and webinars and access online resources to help learn about self-care and support for one another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers are encouraged to share their concerns with their supervisors and school leaders or with the superintendent overseeing their school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They can also tap on other channels for support, such as the school’s Wellness Ambassadors, MOE’s in-house professional counselling services and the 24/7 whole-of-Government counselling hotline.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Beyond MOE and schools, our parents and other stakeholders can also play critical roles in supporting our teachers’ well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, by respecting teachers’ personal time and minimising non-critical communication with teachers outside work hours, parents and the public can also work closely with teachers to establish positive partnerships and set appropriate expectations on the teachers’ responsibilities for our children’s development.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This will ensure that teaching continues to be a meaningful and fulfilling career and that we can continue to attract and retain good teachers to help mould the future of our nation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, we fully support what the Ministry has been doing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: All of us in this House would have spoken to or know many teachers who are in the service.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What they do not like is the administrative part of things and my first supplementary question to the Minister is that we continue to focus more on the relentless effort to reduce their administrative duties because less is always more.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am also happy to note that the Minister talked about how parents can help in this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This is one area which I hope that, for the many parents out there, beyond saying what parents could help, maybe we could consider drawing clear boundaries on where parents should not or cannot do because I think many teachers that I spoke to also said that one of the things that stress them is what parents are imposing on them, either directly or indirectly.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, could the Minister consider drawing up a very clear set of rules on what can and cannot be done, as far as parents are concerned, to the teachers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I remind Members to keep your supplementary questions uncluttered?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, on the first supplementary question, we will continue to do what we can to recruit more quality teachers for our education system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will also do what we can to recruit more allied educators to help our teachers in taking care of the school and the children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But let me maybe just put in context some of the progress that we have made.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we have made progress and we hope to be able to continue to recruit good quality teachers to take care of our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we do what we can to try to improve the numbers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second part is that we also want to streamline many of the processes that we have so that we do not take up this capacity because one of the challenges that we have now is that we have to reinvest the capacity in helping our teachers themselves grow and learn so that they can bring on board with them new experiences, new perspectives to enrich the teaching of our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, as suggested by Mr Seah Kian Peng, we also have higher-needs students and families and special needs children that we want to take better care of, and we also need to manage the socioemotional development of many more children and families.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are places where we need to reinvest the capacity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the Member's second supplementary question about the rules for parents – if you like, the dos and don'ts – yes, indeed, MOE has a set of rules and guidelines for all our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We communicate these rules to the public and our parents and we hope that our parents will also work with the schools to bring this about.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If I may say so, I would like to put in context that not all parents are difficult.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We certainly have our fair share of them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But, perhaps, one difficult parent can take up a substantial amount of time from the teachers, which then makes it unfair for the teachers to take care of the rest.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But just to pay tribute to some of the parent support groups which have done well in this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have many examples of parent support groups – and I have met them recently – who have come forward to help the teachers and the schools to manage many of these things – from curriculum to how to role model a positive relationship between parents and teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, Admiralty Secondary School, Crest Secondary School and Fuhua Primary School all have very strong parent support groups which work with the teachers to bring about a better outcome in our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, we also have many schools with very strong alumni groups which have also contributed much to the schools to alleviate the load on the teachers as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, it is true that there are some parents who may not abide by some of the rules in this code of conduct that we have mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some negative examples would be like going after the teachers for the slightest of issues which require the teachers to spend an inordinate amount of time to try to answer those questions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Once, I met a principal and she told me that she has to deploy her teachers on "corridor" duties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I asked "What are corridor duties?" I understand canteen duties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I was a bit intrigued by corridor duties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And she said that, "Well, just in case the child falls down and the parents want to know what happened.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Otherwise, the parents might be quite upset." So, I think we need to have shared expectations of what we expect from our teachers and what we should not expect our teachers to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Perhaps, in the larger scheme of things, sometimes, it is useful for us to take a step back and ask ourselves what is the kind of environment we want in the schools in order for us to bring up our children who are independent, resilient and creative.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, sometimes, if we overdo things by removing all uncertainties, difficulties and untidiness from the child's life, it may not be the best way for us to bring up our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the other hand, when a child encounters a difficulty and if we, as parents, prematurely step in too often, it may also deprive our children of the ability to deal with some of these difficult situations, including working in teams for project work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we take Mr Seah Kian Peng's points very seriously because such clear expectations on the roles of the teachers are very important for that healthy relationship between parents and teachers and, at the same time, for our teachers to manage their time well.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for his answers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we have been pretty fortunate and will continue to intensify efforts to make sure that we continue to have a fair share of the best people in every cohort to become teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second supplementary question, I have addressed it earlier.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, we will also work to streamline our own processes to make sure that we make the best use of the resources available, besides the structures and organisation issues, then we go back to the issues of how we build this shared relationship with parents and the community to bring out the best in our children.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My supplementary question pertains to seeking the Minister to share whether more of such benefits will also apply to the MOE-seconded teachers in Special Education Schools.
